phases.name: Pre-Drywall: Fireblocking, Backing, Air Sealing & Insulation

checkpoints.name: Building permit issued
checkpoints.desc: Permit issued and permit card posted. Record permit number in project jurisdiction details.

checkpoints.name: Trade permits issued (electrical / plumbing / mechanical / gas)
checkpoints.desc: Who issues trade permits varies in Tennessee (local codes department vs. State Fire Marshal electrical program). Usually pulled by the licensed trade.

checkpoints.name: Hazardous materials clearance (asbestos / lead / mold)
checkpoints.desc: Survey results reviewed; any required abatement completed with clearance documentation before disturbance.

checkpoints.name: Tennessee 811 locate tickets clear
checkpoints.w: A.waterService || A.sewerLateral==='replace' || (A.foundation==='basement' && ['exterior-membrane','both'].includes(A.bsmtWater)) || A.flatwork || A.fence || A.grading || A.porch==='new-deck' || A.porch==='new-porch' || A.gas==='new-service' || A.landscaping
checkpoints.desc: All member utilities have responded / marked before excavation. Keep ticket numbers in notes.

checkpoints.name: Pre-pour slab inspection (base, vapor retarder, reinforcement)
Gas piping rough / pressure test inspection
Pinestone pre-drywall QC sign-off
checkpoints.desc: Internal hold point. Drywall may not be hung until the pre-drywall walkthrough and photo record are complete.

checkpoints.name: Shower waterproofing flood test
checkpoints.desc: Internal hold point per bathroom (some AHJs also inspect pans — confirm). Tile may not start until passed.

q: Every room photographed (4 walls + ceiling + floor)
Exterior elevations, roof, foundation, crawl/attic photographed
Meter, panel, water heater, HVAC data plates photographed
Existing damage documented before work starts

G.w: Document the house as purchased/contracted before any work so pre-existing damage, layout, and utilities are on record.
t: P||Photograph data plates (panel, water heater, furnace/air handler, condenser) — model and age drive scope.
P||Note sagging floors, cracks, water stains, and roof leaks with location tags.
P||Check for active leaks and turn off water if the house is vacant and at risk of freezing.
m: Skipping crawlspace and attic photos — the most common source of later disputes and change orders.
Not recording existing neighbor-side conditions (fences, driveways) before equipment arrives.

q: Joist direction and bearing walls marked

tasks.t: Finalize scope of work & selections schedule

q: Asbestos survey of materials to be disturbed

G.w: Determine whether materials that will be disturbed contain asbestos or lead and whether abatement or lead-safe practices are required before demolition.
t: C|EPA 40 CFR Part 745 (RRP Rule)|Renovation of pre-1978 target housing that disturbs painted surfaces above de minimis thresholds must be performed by an EPA (or authorized-state) certified firm using lead-safe work practices, unless a certified inspector/risk assessor determines no lead-based paint is present.
L||Asbestos survey and notification requirements for residential demolition/renovation depend on building type and program (TDEC / local air program). Confirm before demolition.
P||Pinestone standard: test suspect materials (vermiculite, 9×9 floor tile, mastic, popcorn ceiling, duct wrap, plaster/joint compound) before full gut on any pre-1980s house.
m: Starting demolition on a pre-1978 house without RRP certification or documentation.
Assuming popcorn ceiling or floor mastic is asbestos-free.
G.i: Clearance documentation is recorded on the Hazardous materials clearance checkpoint, separate from this task.

tasks.t: Engage engineer: structural design / stamped letter
q: Beam size, species/grade, bearing and post design specified
Footing / point-load path to foundation specified

G.w: Obtain engineered design for bearing-wall removal, beams, ceiling vaulting, foundation repairs, or other structural changes.
t: C|IRC R301.1.3|Elements not conforming to the prescriptive provisions of the IRC must be designed per accepted engineering practice. Bearing-wall removal with a new beam typically falls here.
P||Ask the engineer to specify: beam, posts, bearing length, squash blocks, foundation/footing at point loads, hangers/straps, and temporary shoring.
L||Some AHJs require a stamped letter or sealed drawings at permit; others accept a site letter afterwards. Confirm.
m: Sizing a beam off a span chart but ignoring the point load path down to the footing.
Ordering an LVL before the engineer confirms ply count and bearing.

q: Window/door schedule incl. egress & safety glazing

G.w: Obtain design approval before exterior changes (windows, siding, roofing, porches).
t: L||Overlay and HOA rules are local. Approved materials and window types may be restricted. Get approval in writing.

tasks.t: Apply for building permit & coordinate trade permits
q: Code edition confirmed and recorded in project
Trade contractors pulling their own permits confirmed

G.w: Apply for the building permit and make sure every licensed trade pulls the permits they are responsible for.
t: L|TN State Fire Marshal / local codes|Tennessee has a state residential program (2018 IRC adopted statewide) but many cities and counties enforce their own adopted edition. Confirm who the AHJ is for this address and record the code edition on the project.
L||Electrical permits/inspections may be issued by the local codes department or by the State Fire Marshal program depending on location.
m: Assuming the city adopted the same edition as the state.
Letting a sub start work before their trade permit is issued.

tasks.w: A.waterService || A.sewerLateral==='replace' || (A.foundation==='basement' && ['exterior-membrane','both'].includes(A.bsmtWater)) || A.flatwork || A.fence || A.grading || A.porch==='new-deck' || A.porch==='new-porch' || A.gas==='new-service' || A.landscaping

G.w: Request utility locates before any digging: sewer/water lines, footings, drainage, fence posts, grading, or flatwork.
t: C|TN Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act (T.C.A. Title 65, Ch. 31)|Excavators must notify the one-call center before excavating and wait the required notice period (working days). Confirm the current notice period and ticket life with Tennessee 811.
P||Private lines (owner sewer laterals, private electric to outbuildings, irrigation) are not marked by 811 — locate them separately.
m: Letting the ticket expire before digging.
Assuming 811 marks the private sewer lateral.

tasks.t: Utility coordination: temp power, disconnects, accounts
q: Service upgrade requested with utility (if any)
License verified (TN Board for Licensing Contractors / local)
COI with general liability on file
Workers comp or exemption on file

tasks.t: Order long-lead items (windows, doors, cabinets, tile, equipment)
q: Window/door sizes verified against rough openings or measured openings

tasks.t: Post permit card, jobsite sign, lockbox

q: Placement does not block sidewalk / ROW without permit

tasks.t: Shut off / make safe utilities in demo areas
q: Circuits in demo areas de-energized and verified dead
Water capped at fixtures or shut at main
Gas shut off and capped at appliances being removed

G.w: Make demolition areas safe: verified-dead circuits, capped water and gas.
t: P||Verify dead with a tester — breaker labels on old panels are unreliable.
P||Leave one labeled temporary circuit or temp pole for tools/lights.
L||Gas shutoffs at the meter may require the utility; capping appliance stubs is licensed gas work.
m: Cutting into a wall with a live circuit fed from an unlabeled breaker.
Leaving gas lines uncapped after appliance removal.

tasks.t: Protect retained items (floors, windows, trees, equipment)
Erosion & sediment control where soil is disturbed
tasks.w: A.waterService || A.sewerLateral==='replace' || (A.foundation==='basement' && ['exterior-membrane','both'].includes(A.bsmtWater)) || A.flatwork || A.fence || A.grading || A.porch==='new-deck' || A.porch==='new-porch' || A.gas==='new-service' || A.landscaping

G.w: Install silt fence / inlet protection where grading or excavation could move soil off site.
t: L||Local stormwater rules vary; small residential lots may still need silt fence or inlet protection.

q: Containment, signage and HEPA cleanup in place

G.w: Set up lead-safe work-area containment for pre-1978 work unless lead-free determination is documented.
t: C|EPA 40 CFR 745 Subpart E|Post warning signs, contain the work area, prohibit dry sanding/open-flame removal, and perform cleaning verification.
P||Keep RRP records (certificates, Renovate Right acknowledgment, cleaning verification) with the project.

tasks.t: Asbestos / lead abatement by licensed contractor

G.w: Licensed abatement of identified materials with clearance documentation before general demolition.
t: L||Licensing, notification, and clearance requirements depend on material and program (TDEC / local). Follow the survey and abatement contractor.

q: Bearing walls identified and NOT removed

G.w: Remove interior finishes to studs and joists within scope without damaging structure or retained elements.
t: P||Mark all bearing walls with paint before demo crews start. Nothing structural comes out during demo — beam work is done by framers under the engineered design.
P||Remove nails/screws from studs and joists as you go (makes framing QC and drywall faster).
m: Removing a bearing wall or cutting joists during demo.
Dropping debris into the crawlspace or open ducts.

q: Abandoned gas lines capped at source by licensed trade

G.w: Remove chimney and fireplace safely and frame/flash the roof and floor openings.
t: P||Plan the roof patch and decking with the roofer; temporary dry-in the same day.
P||Verify whether the chimney carries other flues (furnace/water heater) before removal.

tasks.t: Post-demo photo documentation of all framing
q: Every wall and ceiling bay photographed
Damage (rot, termites, fire, cut joists) photographed with location
Undersized headers / prior bad modifications found
Moisture readings of framing at wet areas

G.w: Walk the open framing to find hidden damage and prior poor work before new work covers it.
t: C|IRC R502.8 / R602.6|Existing notches and bored holes must be within the allowable limits for joists and studs; repair or reinforce those that are not.
P||Take moisture meter readings at sill plates, bath floors, and around old window openings. Wood at or above about 19% MC needs investigation before closing in.
m: Covering damaged framing because it was not in the original scope.

G.w: Treat active infestations and protect new wood.
t: C|IRC R318|Termite protection is required in areas subject to termite damage — Tennessee is in a high-hazard region. Confirm treatment method with the AHJ and licensed pest control.

tasks.t: Update scope & change orders from discoveries
Excavate footings / pier pads for new point loads
q: Size and depth per engineer / IRC R403
Bottom on undisturbed soil, no water

G.w: Dig footings for new posts/piers and point loads before the footing inspection.
t: C|IRC R403.1|Footings sized for loads and soil bearing; bottom below frost depth per local design criteria (Table R301.2(1)).
L||Frost depth is set by the AHJ (Middle Tennessee is commonly 12 in. — confirm).
P||Photograph each hole with a tape measure showing width and depth.

q: Old insulation and vapor barrier removed
Moisture content of sill, joists, girders recorded
Joist clearance to grade checked (18 in. / 12 in. girders)
Dryer, bath fan, plumbing vents not terminating in crawl

G.w: Measure moisture, find rot and water entry, and confirm clearances before crawlspace work is designed.
t: C|IRC R317.1|Wood joists closer than 18 in. or girders closer than 12 in. to exposed ground in crawlspaces must be naturally durable or preservative-treated.
C|IRC R408.4|Crawlspace access opening minimum 18 in. × 24 in. (verify for your foundation type).
P||Record a relative-humidity reading and photo of the hygrometer — use it as a baseline for post-work comparison.

tasks.t: Replace rotted sill plate / rim joist
q: Anchor bolts / approved anchors at required spacing

G.w: Replace damaged sill and rim while temporarily supporting the structure.
t: C|IRC R317.1|Sills on concrete or masonry in contact with the ground must be preservative-treated or naturally durable.
C|IRC R403.1.6|Sill plates anchored to the foundation (bolt size, spacing within 12 in. of plate ends, etc.). Retrofit anchors must be approved / listed.
M||Use corrosion-resistant fasteners rated for the treated lumber used.

q: Sister bears on the same supports as the original (full length) unless engineered

G.w: Reinforce or replace damaged and over-notched joists.
t: P||Full-length sisters bearing on the girder and sill are the Pinestone default. Partial sisters need an engineered detail.
C|IRC R502.8|Cuts, notches and holes in joists limited by size and location — fix prior violations rather than adding new ones.

tasks.t: Shim / adjust supports and level floors
q: Steel shims / hardwood shims (no softwood, no stacked scraps)
Floors checked with laser before and after
Panel span rating matches joist spacing

G.w: Install new subfloor flat and squeak-free for tile and hard-surface flooring.
t: C|IRC R503|Floor sheathing span rating and fastening per IRC tables for the joist spacing.
M||Panel edge spacing and adhesive per panel manufacturer (APA guidelines).
S|TCNA / ANSI|Tile areas need adequate deflection performance (ceramic L/360, natural stone L/720 typical). Plan underlayment accordingly.
m: Nailing with smooth-shank nails into old dried joists (squeaks).
Leaving subfloor uncovered in rain for days.

q: Liner run up piers/walls as designed
No tears; liner protected at access path

G.w: Cover exposed ground in the crawlspace with a continuous vapor retarder.
t: C|IRC R408.2|In vented crawlspaces, required ventilation area can be reduced when the ground surface is covered with a Class I vapor retarder.
C|IRC R408.3|Unvented crawlspaces require a continuous Class I vapor retarder with joints overlapped 6 in. and sealed or taped, edges extended at least 6 in. up the stem wall and attached and sealed.
P||Pinestone standard liner: reinforced 10–20 mil for encapsulation; minimum 6 mil poly for vented crawls.
m: Installing liner before plumbing and framing repairs are done (gets torn).
Leaving liner unsealed at piers and walls in an unvented crawl.

q: Discharge carried well away from foundation
Pump on dedicated / GFCI receptacle as required

tasks.t: Seal crawlspace vents, rim, and penetrations

G.w: Air-seal the crawlspace from the outdoors once penetrations are done.
t: C|IRC R408.3|Unvented crawlspaces: no ventilation openings to the outside; perimeter walls insulated; and one of the listed conditioning methods required.
P||Do this after plumbing, electrical and HVAC have finished in the crawl — otherwise seals get broken.

G.w: Provide the conditioning method required for an unvented crawlspace.
t: C|IRC R408.3|Options include continuously operated mechanical exhaust, conditioned supply air (with return path), or a dehumidifier (added in later editions) at the rates stated in the code. Check which options your adopted edition allows.
M||Dehumidifier condensate routed to sump or drain; dedicated circuit per manufacturer.

tasks.t: Verify foundation vent area & clear vents

G.w: Confirm adequate, unobstructed cross ventilation in a vented crawlspace.
t: C|IRC R408.1 / R408.2|Ventilation openings sized at 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of crawlspace area (reduced to 1 per 1,500 with a Class I ground vapor retarder), one within 3 ft of each corner, with corrosion-resistant screening.

G.w: Insulate the floor (vented crawl) or the foundation walls/rim (unvented crawl).
t: C|IRC N1102.2.7 / N1102.2.11|Floor insulation installed in permanent contact with the underside of the subfloor; crawlspace wall insulation permitted in lieu of floor insulation when the crawl is unvented and meets R408.3.
C|IRC R316|Foam plastic in crawlspaces needs the required thermal/ignition barrier unless listed for exposed use.
L|IRC R318.4|Foam on foundation walls in termite-prone areas may require an inspection gap or other termite provisions. Confirm with AHJ.
m: Floor batts sagging away from the subfloor — no support wires/straps.
Unrated foam left exposed in the crawl.

tasks.t: Scan slab before cutting (post-tension / embedded lines)

G.w: Locate tendons, radiant tubing, conduits and pipes before saw-cutting.
t: P||Check for post-tension stamps or tendon ends at the slab edge. Never cut a post-tensioned slab without engineer direction.

tasks.t: Backfill, compact & vapor retarder in trenches
New slab: base, vapor retarder, reinforcement

G.w: Prepare a new slab section ready for pre-pour inspection.
t: C|IRC R506.2.2 / R506.2.3|Base course and a 6-mil vapor retarder with lapped joints required under slabs on grade over habitable space (with listed exceptions).
P||Photograph vapor retarder laps and reinforcement before the pour.

G.w: Install the radon vent pipe route and suction point (passive or active).
t: L|IRC Appendix F|Radon-resistant construction is in an IRC appendix that applies only where adopted locally. Many Middle Tennessee counties are EPA Radon Zone 1 — Pinestone recommends testing.
P||Label the vent pipe and leave a junction box in the attic for a future fan if passive.

G.w: Excavate, waterproof and drain the foundation from the exterior.
t: C|IRC R406.2 / R405|Waterproofing required for foundation walls enclosing habitable space where high water table conditions exist; foundation drains required around foundations retaining earth and enclosing habitable space (with exceptions).
M||Membrane, protection board and drain mat per manufacturer.

G.w: Cut and install a code-compliant emergency escape opening for the finished basement.
t: C|IRC R310.1 / R310.2|Emergency escape and rescue opening: minimum net clear opening (5.7 sq ft; 5.0 sq ft at grade floor), minimum 24 in. height and 20 in. width, and maximum 44 in. sill height above the floor.
C|IRC R310.2.3|Window wells: minimum 9 sq ft with 36 in. projection/width; ladder or steps when well is deeper than 44 in.
P||Have the engineer confirm the header for the cut foundation opening.

G.w: Frame and insulate basement walls without trapping moisture.
t: P||Use foam against concrete (or a capillary break) and treated bottom plates. Avoid interior poly vapor barriers over concrete walls.
C|IRC R316|Foam plastics need a thermal barrier (typically 1/2 in. gypsum) on the interior.

G.w: Support floor/roof loads on both sides of the bearing wall before it is removed.
t: P||Shore walls on both sides, bearing on solid floor framing or posts down to grade where loads are large. Check what is under the shores.
P||Do not release shoring until beam, posts, connectors and point-load blocking are complete.

tasks.t: Install beam, posts & bearing per engineered design
q: Beam size / plies / grade match the stamped design
Posts plumb and continuous to foundation

G.w: Install the engineered beam and support posts with complete bearing and connections.
t: C|IRC R301.1.3|Engineered elements must be installed as designed. Deviations require engineer approval.
M||LVL / PSL fastening of multiple plies per manufacturer or engineer schedule.
P||Photograph beam stamp/label, ply nailing, bearing, and posts before covering.
m: Posts landing on subfloor with no blocking or footing below.
Missing ply fastening on multi-ply LVL.

tasks.t: Verify continuous load path & squash blocks

G.w: Confirm every new point load is carried through floor framing to a footing.
t: P||Install solid blocking / squash blocks under every post through each floor level down to the girder or footing.

tasks.t: Frame new / enlarged exterior openings (headers, jacks, kings)
q: Header size per R602.7 tables or engineer
Wall bracing compensated where panels removed

G.w: Cut and frame new or resized exterior openings.
t: C|IRC R602.7|Header sizes and jack/king stud counts per the header span tables based on loads above.
C|IRC R602.10|Removing sheathing/wall length can reduce required wall bracing. Confirm bracing still meets the prescriptive requirements or have it engineered.
M||Rough opening size per the window/door manufacturer (typically unit size + 1/2 in.).

G.w: Repair or reinforce rafters, ridge and rafter ties.
t: C|IRC R802|Rafter ties / ceiling joists resist rafter thrust. Do not remove ceiling joists or collar/rafter ties without an engineered alternative (ridge beam).

tasks.t: Vaulted / raised ceiling framing per design

q: Riser max 7-3/4 in., tread min 10 in.

G.w: Frame new or altered stairs to code geometry.
t: C|IRC R311.7|Stair width, headroom (6 ft 8 in.), riser height (7-3/4 in. max), tread depth (10 in. min), and uniformity (3/8 in. tolerance).
P||Lay out with finished floor thickness top and bottom — the most common cause of non-uniform first/last risers.

tasks.t: New interior partition walls / layout changes

G.w: Provide a compliant attic access.
t: C|IRC R807.1|Attic access minimum 22 in. × 30 in. rough opening with 30 in. headroom above, located in a hallway or readily accessible location.
C|IRC N1102.2.4|Access hatches/doors to be weatherstripped and insulated to the level of the surrounding surface (energy code).

tasks.t: Straighten / plane walls & ceilings for flat drywall
q: Kitchen cabinet walls within 1/8 in. in 8 ft
Tile walls flat for large-format tile
Ceiling joists planed / furred where crowned

G.w: Fix crowned, bowed and twisted framing before rough-ins so drywall, tile and cabinets come out flat.
t: P||Use a long straightedge / string line on every kitchen and tile wall. Sister or plane — do not rely on drywall mud.
S|TCNA|Large-format tile substrates require tighter flatness (commonly 1/8 in. in 10 ft).

tasks.t: Bath framing: tub/shower walls, curbs, niches, recesses
q: Niche framed to tile module, not on exterior wall
Curb / curbless recess per waterproofing system

G.w: Frame the bathroom for the selected tub/shower and waterproofing system.
t: M||Curbless showers: recess and slope per the system manufacturer. Recessing joists requires an engineered solution (do not just cut joists down).
P||Frame niches to the tile layout — set the niche top/bottom on a full or half tile line. Avoid niches on exterior walls (insulation and condensation).
m: Cutting floor joists to recess a curbless shower without engineering.
Niche sized without looking at the tile module.

q: Every hanger nail hole filled with specified nails

G.w: Install all specified hangers, straps and hold-downs with the correct fasteners.
t: M||Install per the connector manufacturer (e.g. Simpson Strong-Tie) catalog: specified nail size/quantity — never drywall or deck screws.
C|IRC R317.3|Fasteners and connectors in contact with preservative-treated wood must be of the required corrosion-resistance.
P||Photograph connectors at the beam and posts with the nail pattern visible.
m: Half-nailed hangers.
Using a top-flange hanger where face-mount was specified.

q: Panel edges on rafters, H-clips if required by span

G.w: Install underlayment, eave/valley protection and drip edge per code and the shingle/metal manufacturer.
t: C|IRC R905.2.7 / R905.2.8.5|Underlayment and drip edge required for asphalt shingles (drip edge at eaves and gables).
L|IRC R905.1.2|Ice barrier at eaves is required only where there has been a history of ice forming along the eaves — determined by the AHJ.
M||Underlayment type, laps and fastening per roofing manufacturer to keep the warranty.

tasks.t: Roof flashing: step, counter, kickout, valleys, pipe boots
q: Kickout flashing at every roof-to-wall termination

G.w: Flash all roof transitions so water is directed onto the roof surface, not into walls.
t: C|IRC R903.2|Flashing required at wall and roof intersections, changes of slope/direction, and around roof openings; kickout flashing where the eave of a roof intersects a wall.
M||Shingle manufacturer step-flashing and valley details.
m: Missing kickout flashing — causes hidden wall rot below roof/wall intersections.
Reusing old cracked pipe boots.

G.w: Provide balanced intake and exhaust attic ventilation.
t: C|IRC R806.1 / R806.2|Net free ventilating area 1/150 of the vented space, or 1/300 when conditions in R806.2 are met (e.g. upper/lower vent distribution).
C|IRC R806.3|Maintain at least 1 in. of airspace between insulation and roof sheathing at the vent — install baffles.
P||Do not mix ridge vents with gable or powered vents (short-circuits the ridge).

G.w: Install a continuous weather-resistive barrier integrated with all flashings.
t: C|IRC R703.2|A water-resistive barrier is required over sheathing behind exterior veneer, lapped and continuous to the top of walls and terminated at penetrations and building appendages.
M||Housewrap laps, fasteners, and tape per manufacturer.

q: Sill pan / sloped sill flashing installed
Jamb flashing then head flashing (shingle order)
Shimmed at manufacturer locations, operable & square

G.w: Install windows plumb, level and square with a flashing sequence that drains water to the exterior.
t: C|IRC R703.4|Flashing required at window and door openings, installed to prevent water entry into the wall cavity and per the fenestration manufacturer instructions (or pan flashing / flashing details where no instructions are provided).
M||Installation instructions of the specific window: sill pan, shim points, fastening, sealant. Deviations can void the warranty.
C|IRC R308.4|Safety glazing in hazardous locations (e.g. within 24 in. of doors, large panes near floors, at tubs/showers, at stairs).
m: Taping the sill flange (traps water). Leave the bottom of the sill flashing unsealed to drain or follow the manufacturer.
Over-driving fasteners and racking the frame.

tasks.t: Verify egress, safety glazing & fall protection

G.w: Check every sleeping room window and hazardous location after installation.
t: C|IRC R310|Sleeping rooms require an emergency escape opening meeting net clear opening and sill height limits. Replacement windows have an exception (R310.2.5) for existing openings — confirm with the AHJ.
C|IRC R312.2|Window fall protection where the opening is less than 24 in. above the floor and more than 72 in. above grade.
C|IRC R308.4 / R308.1|Safety glazing labeled in all hazardous locations.

tasks.t: Install exterior doors (sill pan, flashing, threshold)

G.w: Prove the openings and roof are watertight before insulation and drywall.
t: P||Spray test a sample of windows and every door from the bottom up while someone watches the interior side. Check after the first heavy rain.

G.w: Walk every fixture location with the plumber before rough-in using the actual fixture specifications.
t: P||Bring spec sheets for every fixture: rough-in heights for vanity drains and supplies, valve depth range, toilet rough distance, freestanding tub drain location.
C|IRC R307.1|Fixture clearances: water closet centerline 15 in. min to a side wall/obstruction, 21 in. clear in front; 24 in. clear in front of shower openings.

tasks.t: New water service line (meter to house)

G.w: Replace the service line with proper depth, sleeving and a main shutoff.
t: L||Pipe depth, tracer wire, and meter-side work responsibility are set by the water utility and AHJ.
C|IRC P2903.3 / P2903.9|Pressure must not exceed 80 psi static at fixtures (install a PRV if higher); main shutoff valve required.

G.w: Camera the lateral to the main; replace or repair as needed.
t: P||Save the camera video file and footage locations. Scope again after replacement.
L||Connections in the right-of-way often require a separate utility permit / inspection.

q: Slope 1/4 in./ft (≤2-1/2 in.) or 1/8 in./ft (≥3 in.)

G.w: Install drain, waste and vent piping with correct slope, venting and accessible cleanouts.
t: C|IRC P3005.3|Horizontal drainage slope: 1/4 in. per foot for pipe 2-1/2 in. and smaller; 1/8 in. per foot for 3 in. and larger.
C|IRC P3005.2|Cleanouts required (e.g. at base of stacks, changes of direction over 45°, every 100 ft) and must be accessible.
L|IRC P3114|Air admittance valves are allowed by the IRC but local acceptance varies; confirm before relying on them (islands).
m: Flat drain runs to make a joist cut easier.
Burying cleanouts behind drywall or tile with no access panel.

tasks.t: Water supply rough-in (manifold, home runs, shutoffs)
q: PEX supported per manufacturer, no kinks

tasks.t: Nail plates at all pipes within 1-1/4 in. of framing face

G.w: Protect piping from drywall and trim fasteners.
t: C|IRC P2603.2.1|Pipes passing through framing within 1-1/4 in. of the edge (or notched) must be protected by steel shield plates at least 1/16 in. thick (0.0575 in.) extending 2 in. beyond the pipe (verify dimensions in your edition).
P||Plate both faces at every bore near the edge, including top/bottom plates at stacks.
m: Missing plates at vanity walls and toilet supplies — classic drywall-screw leak.

tasks.t: Verify bored / notched framing within limits
q: Top plates cut >50% tied with metal strap
Joist holes not in top/bottom 2 in. or near bearing

G.w: Walk all framing after trades bore and notch; repair violations before inspection.
t: C|IRC R602.6|Bearing-wall studs: notches ≤25% of width, bored holes ≤40% (≤60% when doubled), holes ≥5/8 in. from the edge.
C|IRC R602.6.1|Top plates cut more than 50% need a 16-ga. steel tie (1-1/2 in. wide) with fasteners each side.
C|IRC R502.8|Joist notches/holes limited in size and location (no notches in middle third; holes ≤1/3 depth, ≥2 in. from edges).

q: Air barrier behind tub on exterior walls

G.w: Set the tub before walls so it can be supported, leveled and integrated with waterproofing.
t: M||Mortar bed / support per tub manufacturer (common for acrylic/steel tubs).
C|IRC N1102.4.1.1 (Table)|Exterior walls behind tubs/showers need insulation and an air barrier separating them from the tub.

tasks.t: Shower / tub valve rough: depth, height, pressure-balance
q: Valve depth within manufacturer range for total wall thickness (backer + membrane + tile)
Shower head & handheld heights per layout
